name: Small cell lung cancer
theme: the anti-ticket-rack · tempo is the biology

meta.title: Small cell lung cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Small cell lung cancer (limited and extensive stage), adult
meta.population: Adults with SCLC - the registry's fastest-tempo disease and its deliberate ANTI-ticket-rack: where the NSCLC trainer waits on a ten-door molecular panel, this one has no actionable driver test at all - stage and tempo are the biology, decisions are made in days, and the first treatment usually works before it stops working. Combined SCLC/NSCLC histology is treated as SCLC (note); LCNEC lives in the NSCLC trainer; the main fork is limited stage (one radiation field - now the ADRIATIC era, the first change in 35 years) versus extensive stage (the chemo-immunotherapy-plus-maintenance era, with tarlatamab rewriting the second line).
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease where 2024-2026 delivered both endings of the accelerated-approval story in a single ledger: tarlatamab converted to FULL approval on a randomized OS win over chemotherapy (DeLLphi-304: 13.6 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.60 - the new second-line standard), while lurbinectedin's confirmatory LAGOON failed outright (June 2026, FDA action pending) even as its 1L-maintenance combination earned approval (IMforte, October 2025) - one molecule, one year, one win and one loss. Limited stage carries ADRIATIC (durvalumab consolidation: median OS 55.9 vs 33.4 m…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: LS vs ES pragmatic staging atop formal IASLC/AJCC TNM-9 (effective 2025, applies to SCLC); LS = confined to one hemithorax/encompassable in one radiation field
meta.response: RECIST 1.1; the load-bearing response read is post-chemoradiation status in LS (ADRIATIC's entry ticket) and post-induction status in ES (the maintenance fork)

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: SCLC's paradox: even poor-PS patients often merit treatment, because the disease causing the poor PS is the most chemosensitive solid tumor - performance status here can improve WITH therapy.
Patient.helpPatient: Feeling very unwell from this cancer is often an argument FOR quick treatment, not against it - it responds fast.

Newly diagnosed.name: Concurrent chemoradiation -> durvalumab consolidation (the ADRIATIC era)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized (ADRIATIC) atop level-1 CRT backbone (Turrisi, CONVERT)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the demanding season: esophagitis (27% grade 3 with BID), cytopenias, then two years of immune vigilance - traded for a median survival that nearly doubled
Newly diagnosed.patient: For disease within one radiation field: chemotherapy and radiation together, then up to two years of immunotherapy - the first big advance in this situation in a generation, nearly doubling the middle survival time.

Newly diagnosed.name: Platinum-etoposide + immunotherapy (CASPIAN / IMpower133 - the ES backbone)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - OS met, 3-yr mature
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemotherapy's season (cytopenias dominate) plus the immune ledger - and the response usually comes fast, which is this disease's one kindness
Newly diagnosed.patient: For disease beyond one field: chemotherapy plus immunotherapy - it usually works quickly, and the immunotherapy gives a real minority of patients years.

Newly diagnosed.name: Maintenance lurbinectedin + atezolizumab (IMforte - the held-induction extension)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: FDA-approved maintenance (2025-10, secondhand); NCCN placement evolving
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS and OS met (maintenance-clock numbers)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: adds lurbinectedin's cytopenias to the maintenance rhythm - the price of the extension
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the first phase holds the cancer: adding a second drug to the maintenance immunotherapy kept it held longer and added survival time - the first proven 'keep it away' upgrade in this disease.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; breathlessness and CNS symptom care are the craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice - with the honest note that this particular cancer both moves fastest without treatment and responds fastest to it, so the conversation deserves both halves.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Tarlatamab (DeLLphi-304 - the conversion success; the new 2L standard)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FULL FDA approval 2025-11-19 (secondhand); the evidence-based 2L standard
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS superiority over chemotherapy; conversion completed
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS front-loaded (cycle-1 monitoring), then notably gentler than chemotherapy - the rare 2L where the better drug is also the kinder one
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When this cancer returns: an antibody that recruits your T cells beat chemotherapy on survival itself - five extra months in the middle - while being easier to tolerate. Its approval graduated from provisional to permanent on that proof.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Platinum rechallenge (late sensitive relapse - the old logic still holds)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the familiar chemotherapy season, again - chosen when the first one's durability earned the repeat
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the first chemotherapy's benefit lasted months: running it again often works again - the old, reasonable road, now alongside the newer antibody.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Lurbinectedin monotherapy (the failed confirmatory - the ledger's other ending)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: accelerated approval 2020 (secondhand); CONFIRMATORY FAILED 2026-06 - regulatory status watch
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 basket (accelerated); phase 3 confirmatory NEGATIVE (press-stage, publication pending)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias and fatigue - and now a card whose main content is its own regulatory suspense
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A drug approved provisionally five years ago whose proving trial just failed - it may leave this use soon, and the card says so plainly. (Strangely, the same drug succeeded in a different role - keeping first-line responses held.)

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Topotecan (the honest historical bar)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN-listed 2L (secondhand); the comparator arm of the modern era
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: randomized (1999-era) + the DeLLphi-304 control arm as its modern measurement
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: heavily myelosuppressive - the grade >=3 rate (80% in DeLLphi-304's chemo arm) is the number tarlatamab halved
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The old standard for relapse - real but hard, and now honestly the second choice where the newer antibody is available.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged); the CM331/451 negatives verified
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort at relapse is a real road - chosen with the true numbers, and with symptom care that this disease's tempo makes especially valuable.

refs.label: NCI PDQ: Small Cell Lung Cancer Treatment (HP, updated 2025-05-14, loaded live 2026-08) - LS/ES framing, combined-histology-as-SCLC, and the ADRIATIC 'first new option in over 35 years' language

Turrisi et al. Twice-daily (45 Gy/3 wk) vs once-daily thoracic RT concurrent with cisplatin-etoposide in LS-SCLC: median OS 23 vs 19 months, 5-yr 26% vs 16% (grade 3 esophagitis 27% vs 11%) - the level-1 backbone. NEJM 1999;340:265-71 (PMID 9920950 - a wrong candidate PMID caught this run) | PMID 9920950 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Faivre-Finn et al. CONVERT: 45 Gy BID vs 66 Gy QD concurrent CRT - once-daily NOT superior (median OS 30 vs 25 months favoring BID numerically, p=0.14); both acceptable, BID keeps level-1 status. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1116-25 | PMID 28642008 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Cheng et al. ADRIATIC: durvalumab consolidation after concurrent CRT in LS-SCLC without progression - median OS 55.9 vs 33.4 months (HR 0.73, p=0.01), PFS 16.6 vs 9.2; FDA 2024-12-04 (secondhand); NCCN category 1 (secondhand). NEJM 2024;391:1313-27 (PMID 39268857 - the off-by-one wrong-PMID 39268847 resolves to a conservation-biology paper; caught this run) | PMID 39268857 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Auperin et al. PCI meta-analysis (complete responders, pre-MRI era): death RR 0.84, 3-yr OS +5.4% (15.3->20.7%), brain-met RR 0.46 - the 1999 case FOR. NEJM 1999;341:476-84 | PMID 10441603 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Takahashi et al. PCI vs MRI surveillance in ES-SCLC (MRI-staged): PCI did NOT improve OS (median 11.6 vs 13.7 months, HR 1.27, futility stop) - the MRI-era case AGAINST. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:663-71 | PMID 28343976 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

SWOG S1827 MAVERICK (NCT04155034): MRI surveillance +/- PCI, LS and ES, n=668, phase 3 - CLOSED to accrual 2025-12; primary results NOT public as of 2026-08; plenary listed for ASTRO 2026. The controversy's answer, imminent - registry-verified
Horn et al. IMpower133: atezolizumab + carboplatin-etoposide, 1L ES - OS 12.3 vs 10.3 months (HR 0.70). NEJM 2018;379:2220-9 | PMID 30280641 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Paz-Ares et al. CASPIAN: durvalumab + platinum-etoposide, 1L ES - OS 13.0 vs 10.3 (HR 0.73); 3-yr update: 17.6% vs 5.8% alive - the added long tail. Lancet 2019;394:1929-39 (update ESMO Open 2022) | PMID 31590988 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Paz-Ares et al. IMforte: maintenance lurbinectedin + atezolizumab after held induction - PFS HR 0.54, OS HR 0.73 (13.2 vs 10.6 months from maintenance randomization); approved 2025-10-02 (secondhand) - the first ES maintenance regimen. Lancet 2025;405:2129-43 | PMID 40473449 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Slotman et al. CREST: consolidative thoracic RT in ES responders - 1-yr primary NS; 2-yr OS 13% vs 3% (secondary) - consider in selected responders; pre-IO era, said plainly. Lancet 2015;385:36-42 | PMID 25230595 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Ahn et al. DeLLphi-301: tarlatamab 10 mg - ORR 40%, DOR >=6 months in 59% of responders; CRS 51% (mostly cycle 1) - the accelerated-approval basis (2024-05-16, secondhand). NEJM 2023;389:2063-75 | PMID 37861218 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Mountzios et al. DeLLphi-304: tarlatamab vs chemotherapy (2L) - OS 13.6 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.60, p<0.001), grade >=3 AEs 54% vs 80% - the confirmatory WIN; FULL approval 2025-11-19 (secondhand). The 2L standard. NEJM 2025;393:349-61 | PMID 40454646 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25
Trigo et al. Lurbinectedin basket (B-005): ORR 35%, mDOR 5.3 months - the 2020 accelerated-approval basis. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:645-54 | PMID 32224306 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

LAGOON (NCT05153239) confirmatory phase 3 FAILED its OS endpoint (topline 2026-06-12: neither lurbinectedin mono nor lurbi+irinotecan beat control; combo HR 0.902) - press-stage, publication pending; FDA action on the 2L indication PENDING as of 2026-08. The ledger's other ending (sponsor announcement)

The 2L chemotherapy bar: von Pawel 1999 (topotecan vs CAV - equivalent survival, better symptom control; PMID 10080612 - a wrong candidate PMID caught this run) and O'Brien 2006 (oral topotecan vs BSC: ~doubled survival); measured live by DeLLphi-304's control arm at 8.3 months. JCO 1999;17:658-67 | PMID 10080612 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Spigel et al. CheckMate 331: 2L nivolumab vs chemotherapy - NEGATIVE (OS 7.5 vs 8.4, HR 0.86) - the IO ledger's kept failure. Ann Oncol 2021;32:631-41 | PMID 33539946 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Owonikoko et al. CheckMate 451: maintenance nivolumab +/- ipilimumab - NEGATIVE (OS HR 0.92) - checkpoint inhibitors alone never earned a maintenance role. JCO 2021;39:1349-59 | PMID 33683919 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Rudin et al. SCLC molecular subtypes (ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3/YAP1) - research framework, no treatment selection (until PRISM); Nat Rev Cancer 2019;19:289-97 (PMID 30926931 - a wrong candidate PMID caught this run)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.
TIGOS-LS (NCT06773910): atigotatug+nivolumab vs durvalumab consolidation after concurrent CRT, LS-SCLC, randomized phase 2, OS primary, 33 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08

DeLLphi-312 (NCT07005128): 1L tarlatamab + durvalumab-carboplatin-etoposide vs backbone alone, ES-SCLC, phase 3 (dual OS/PFS primaries), 51 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08 (DeLLphi-305/-306 both closed to accrual)

DAREON-5 (NCT05882058): obrixtamig (BI 764532, DLL3 engager), R/R ES-SCLC >=2 lines, prior DLL3-engager EXCLUDED, phase 2, 13 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08. No recruiting post-tarlatamab trial exists (REPLAT is not-yet-recruiting, Germany)

SWOG PRISM / S2409 (NCT06769126): subtype-directed maintenance (ASCL1/NEUROD1xSLFN11 -> PARPi; SLFN11-neg -> ATRi; inflamed -> NKG2A) on durvalumab backbone, ES-SCLC, randomized phase 2 multicohort, ~140 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08

CMS NCD 210.14 Lung Cancer Screening with Low Dose Computed Tomography (LDCT) — annual LDCT covered for beneficiaries age 50-77 with at least a 20 pack-year smoking history who currently smoke or quit within the last 15 years and are asymptomatic; requires a counseling and shared decision-making visit before first screen; effective February 10, 2022 (fetched 2026-09-09).

CMS NCD 310.1 Routine Costs in Clinical Trials — Medicare covers routine costs of qualifying clinical trials and items/services to diagnose and treat complications arising from trial participation; current version 3 effective May 27, 2024 (re-verified by fetch 2026-09-09).

CMS NCD 90.2 Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) — covers FDA-approved/cleared companion-diagnostic NGS in CLIA-certified labs for patients with recurrent, relapsed, refractory, metastatic, or advanced stage III/IV cancer seeking further treatment; somatic coverage effective March 16, 2018 (re-verified by fetch 2026-09-09).

NCI PDQ Small Cell Lung Cancer Treatment (patient version) — 'a type of fast-growing cancer'; smoking 'the most important risk factor'; limited vs extensive stage; diagnosis via sputum cytology, bronchoscopy, and biopsy; treatments include chemotherapy, radiation, immunotherapy, laser therapy, and endoscopic stent placement (fetched 2026-09-09).

CDC — Lung Cancer Risk Factors: 'Cigarette smoking is the number one risk factor for lung cancer,' linked to about 80% of US lung cancer deaths; radon, secondhand smoke, and workplace exposures also covered (fetched 2026-09-09).

American Cancer Society — What Is Lung Cancer?: 'About 10% to 15% of all lung cancers are SCLC'; 'tends to grow and spread faster than NSCLC'; 'tends to respond well to chemotherapy and radiation therapy' but usually returns (fetched 2026-09-09).

American Cancer Society — Signs and Symptoms of Lung Cancer: paraneoplastic syndromes of SCLC including SIADH ('the cancer cells make ADH'), ectopic-ACTH Cushing syndrome, and Lambert-Eaton syndrome; superior vena cava syndrome (fetched 2026-09-09).
